Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 83, verses 1–14:

Makkiyya? No: it is Madaniyya (Medinan), and it has thirty-six verses, one hundred and sixty-nine words, and seven hundred and thirty letters.

We were informed by Kamil ibn Ahmad al-Mufid, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Mutar al-'Adl, who said: Ibn Ibrahim ibn Shurayk al-Asadi related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Yarbu'i related to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, who said: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mutaffifin, Allah, glorified is He, will give him to drink from the sealed wine (al-Raheeq al-Makhtum) on the Day of Resurrection" [105] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/289.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Woe to those who give less (al-mutaffifin)﴾. That is, those who diminish people's due and defraud them of their rights in measuring and weighing. The root is from "al-shay' al-tafif," meaning a small, meagre amount, and "inā' tafaff" is a vessel that is not full. From this is said of people who are equal in reckoning or number: "they are like the tafaff of the sa'," meaning: like the nearness of the filling to it, lacking from full measure [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/113.]].

﴿Who, when they take a measure from people, take in full﴾: that is, from them; "'ala" and "min" interchange in this place. ﴿And when they measure or weigh for them﴾: that is, measure for them or weigh for them. It is said: "I weighed you your right" and "I measured you food," meaning "I weighed for you" and "I measured for you." Al-Farra' said: this is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and those beyond them from [......] [[Illegible word in the manuscript.]]. He said: I heard a Bedouin woman say: "When people return from the pilgrimage, we come to the merchant and he measures for us the mudd and the mudds until the next season."

Abu 'Ubayd said: 'Isa ibn 'Umar used to make it two separate words, pausing on "kalaw" and "wazanu," then beginning with "hum yukhsirun." He said: I think the reading of Hamza is also like this. Abu 'Ubayd said: the preferred view is that it is one word, for two reasons. The first: the script, since they wrote it without an alif; had they been two separate words, they would have been written "kalaw" and "wazanu" with an alif, as they wrote all verbs, such as "fa'aw" and "ja'aw" [ ... ] [[Blank space in the manuscript.]]

in the copies of the Qur'an, except for dropping it.

The other reason: it is said "kiltuka" and "wazantuka," meaning "kiltu laka" and "wazantu laka," and this is Arabic speech, just as one says "sadtuka" (I hunted for you) and "sadtu laka," and "kasabtuka" and "kasabtu laka," and there are many similar examples.

﴿Yukhsirun﴾: they diminish.

Abu Muhammad al-Makhlidi related to us, who said: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr related to us, who said:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Yazid al-Nahwi related to me that 'Ikrima related to him from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, they were among the most dishonest people in measuring. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed "Woe to those who give less," and they improved their measuring.

Al-Qurtubi said: In Medina there were merchants who cheated in measure, and their trade was like gambling, the "munabadha" and "mulamasa" and "mukhatara" (types of forbidden sale). So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the market and recited it to them.

Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, and there was a man there called Abu Juhayna, who had two sa's: he measured with one and took measure with the other. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Yusuf related to us, who said: Ibn 'Imran related to us, who said: Abu al-Darda', 'Abd al-'Aziz [ibn Munayb] related to us, who said: Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Kaysan related to us, from his father, from al-Dahhak, Mujahid and Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Five for five." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is five for five?" He said: "No people break a covenant except that their enemy is given power over them; and they do not judge by other than what Allah has revealed except that poverty spreads among them; and indecency does not appear among them except that death spreads among them; and they do not cheat in measure except that they are denied plant growth and are seized by years of drought; and they do not withhold zakat except that rain is withheld from them" [106] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 11/38.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Majah related to us, who said: Ibn Ayyub related to us, who said: al-Qasawani related to us, who said: Sinan ibn Hatim related to us, who said: Hafs related to us, who said: Malik ibn Dinar related to us, who said: I entered upon a neighbour of mine when death had come upon him, and he kept saying: "Two mountains of fire, two mountains of fire." I said: "What are you saying? Are you delirious?"

He said: "O Abu Yahya, I had two measures: I measured with one and took measure with the other." He said: So I got up and began striking one against the other, and he said: "O Abu Yahya, every time you strike one against the other it grows larger," and he died in his pain.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Saqlan related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Naffakh al-Bahili related to us, who said: Barakah ibn Muhammad al-Halabi related to us, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Nadr ibn 'Adi, who said:

I heard 'Ikrima say: "I testify against every measurer or weigher that he is in the Fire." It was said to him: "Your son is a measurer or weigher." He said: "I testify that he is in the Fire."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya al-Qadi related to me, who said: al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us, who said: al-Mubarrad related to us, who said: al-Riyashi related to us, from al-Asma'i, who said: A Bedouin said to me: "Do not seek needs from one whose manliness is at the top of the measures and the teeth of the scales." And 'Abd Khayr related that 'Ali passed by a man who was weighing saffron and had over-weighed it. He tilted the scale and said: "Establish the weighing with justice, then over-weigh afterwards as much as you wish." Nafi' said: Ibn 'Umar used to pass by a seller and say: "Fear Allah and give full measure and weight, for the defrauders will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection until sweat will bridle them up to the middles of their ears."

﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a great Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾? Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Malik related to us, who said: Ibn Hanbal related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Waki' related to us, from Hisham, the companion of [al-Dastawani], from al-Qamar ibn Abi [Abzi], who said: someone who heard Ibn 'Umar recite "Woe to those who give less," when he reached "the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds," wept until they fell down, and he refrained from reciting what followed.

﴿Nay﴾. Al-Hasan said: truly. ﴿Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾: the register in which their deeds are written. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, Mughith ibn Sumayy, Qatada, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: it is the lowest seventh earth, in which are the spirits of the disbelievers and their deeds. What indicates this is what

al-Husayn informed us, who said: Musa related to us, who said: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, who said: Isma'il related to us, who said: al-Musayyib related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sijjin is beneath the seven earths."

[107] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/292; similar in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

And Abu 'Abd Allah al-Fanjawi informed me, who said: Abu 'Ali al-Muqri' related to us, who said: Abu [al-Qasim ibn] al-Fadl related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari related to us, who said: Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Sam'ar ibn 'Atiyya, who said: Ibn 'Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said: "Inform me about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted: 'Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin'." He said: The spirit of the wicked is raised up to the heaven, but the heaven refuses to accept it. Then it is brought down to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it. So it descends beneath the seven earths until it reaches Sijjin, which is the boundary of Iblis. From Sijjin, beneath the boundary of Iblis, there comes out a scroll, which is inscribed and sealed and placed beneath the boundary of Iblis, bearing the knowledge of their ruin until the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also held this view, saying: Sijjin is beneath the boundary of Iblis. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: It is the lowest earth, in which are Iblis and his offspring.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related to us, who said: I read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: 'Imara ibn 'Isa related to me from Yunus ibn Yazid, from one who related to him from Ibn 'Abbas that he said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Inform me about Sijjin and 'Illiyyun." Ka'b said:

"By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will inform you of it only according to what I find in the revealed Book of Allah. As for Sijjin, it is a black tree beneath the seven earths, in which is written every name of a devil. When the soul of the disbeliever is taken, it is raised to the heaven, but the gates of the heaven are shut before it, and then it is thrown down to Sijjin; that is Sijjin. As for 'Illiyyun, when the soul of the Muslim is taken, it is raised to the heaven and the gates of the heaven are opened for it until it reaches the Throne." He said: "Then a palm comes out from the Throne and writes for him his lodging and his honour; that is 'Illiyyun."

Al-Kalbi said: It is a rock beneath the lowest seventh earth, green with the greenness of the heavens, and the book of the wicked is placed beneath it. Wahb said: It is the last domain of Iblis.

'Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa told them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti related to me, who said: Mas'ud ibn Musa ibn Mishkan related to us, who said: Nasr ibn Khuzayma related to us, from Shu'ayb ibn Safwan, from al-Qurti, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Al-Falaq is a well in Hell that is covered, and as for Sijjin, it is a well in Hell that is open." [108] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/120; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/325.]]

Abu al-Qamar al-Saffar informed us, who said: Hajib ibn Ahmad informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us, who said:

Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin." He said: Sijjin is a rock beneath the seventh earth, turned over, and the record of the wicked is placed beneath it. Ikrima said: That is, they are in loss and error. The meaning is that he intended the nullification of their deeds and their passing away without praise or reward, and this is a common and widespread usage among people: they say of one whose mention has faded and whose standing has fallen: "he has clung to the dust." Al-Akhfash said: It is in a narrow, severe prison, and it is of the pattern fa''il from "prison," as one says "fasiq" and "shariyb." Ibn Muqbil said:

"And their companions strike the swords in the bright hour, a striking that the heroes have enjoined upon one another, imprisoning." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ — that is, O Muhammad, what is Sijjin? That is the book that is in Sijjin. Then He explained: ﴿It is a book inscribed﴾: that is, it is a written, recorded book set against them like a mark in a garment, not forgotten and not erased until they are recompensed by it. Qatada said: "marked against them with evil." It was also said: "sealed in the language of Himyar."

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers, who deny the Day of Judgment. None deny it except every transgressor, sinful, who, when Our verses are recited to him, says: "Tales of the ancients."﴾ The common reading is "tutla" (recited); Abu Hayyan read it with the ya', because the verb is placed first.

﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.﴾

We were informed by al-Husayn, who said:

Al-Fadl related to us, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Mukarram al-Tarbi related to us in Baghdad, who said: 'Ali al-Mukarrami related to us, who said: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan say: al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim related to me that Abu Salih al-Sammān said that Abu Hurayra related to him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, when the servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he repents, his heart is polished; if he returns (to sin), it increases until his heart is blackened."

[109] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/297; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 1/25; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/123, with variation.]] He said:

That is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts." And so the exegetes said: it is sin upon sin until the heart is blackened. Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman said: The heart is like the palm; when the servant sins, it contracts and closes one finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes another finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes all its fingers, and then it is sealed. They used to regard that as the "rayn," and then he recited this verse.

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: When the servant commits a sin, it becomes in his heart like the prick of a needle; then when he sins a second time, it becomes like that; when sins multiply, the heart becomes like a sieve or a strainer. al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin, until perhaps it rusts the heart. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He sealed them." 'Ata' said: "They were overcome over their hearts, and so they fell upon them, and so they do not feel alarm or shame." It was also said: "He turned it over, so that its lower part became its upper part," like His saying: "And We turn their hearts about" [[Surat al-An'am: 110.]]. The root of "rayn" is domination; one says: "The wine rayn over his mind" when it overcomes him so that he becomes drunk. Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:

"Then when he sees him, wine has overcome him, and he does not get rid of it by guarding against it."

And the rajiz said:

"We did not drink until I was exiled, and the wine overcame me, and it overcame the cupbearer who was with me."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/122.]]

The meaning of the verse: their hearts were overcome, and it encompassed them until it covered and overwhelmed them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Malik related to us, who said: Ibn Hanbal related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Waki' related to us, from Hisham, the companion of [al-Dastawani], from al-Qamar ibn Abi [Abzi], who said: someone who heard Ibn 'Umar recite "Woe to those who give less," when he reached "the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds," wept until they fell down, and he refrained from reciting what followed.

From this is said of people who are equal in reckoning or number: "they are like the tafaff of the sa'," meaning: like the nearness of the filling to it, lacking from full measure [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 30/113.]].

﴿Who, when they take a measure from people, take in full﴾: that is, from them; "'ala" and "min" interchange in this place. ﴿And when they measure or weigh for them﴾: that is, measure for them or weigh for them. It is said: "I weighed you your right" and "I measured you food," meaning "I weighed for you" and "I measured for you." Al-Farra' said: this is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz and those beyond them from [......] [[Illegible word in the manuscript.]]. He said: I heard a Bedouin woman say: "When people return from the pilgrimage, we come to the merchant and he measures for us the mudd and the mudds until the next season."

Abu 'Ubayd said: 'Isa ibn 'Umar used to make it two separate words, pausing on "kalaw" and "wazanu," then beginning with "hum yukhsirun." He said: I think the reading of Hamza is also like this. in the copies of the Qur'an, except for dropping it.

The other reason: it is said "kiltuka" and "wazantuka," meaning "kiltu laka" and "wazantu laka," and this is Arabic speech, just as one says "sadtuka" (I hunted for you) and "sadtu laka," and "kasabtuka" and "kasabtu laka," and there are many similar examples.

﴿Yukhsirun﴾: they diminish.

Abu Muhammad al-Makhlidi related to us, who said: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr related to us, who said:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Yazid al-Nahwi related to me that 'Ikrima related to him from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, they were among the most dishonest people in measuring. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed "Woe to those who give less," and they improved their measuring.

Al-Qurtubi said: In Medina there were merchants who cheated in measure, and their trade was like gambling, the "munabadha" and "mulamasa" and "mukhatara" (types of forbidden sale). So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the market and recited it to them.

Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, and there was a man there called Abu Juhayna, who had two sa's: he measured with one and took measure with the other. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Yusuf related to us, who said: Ibn 'Imran related to us, who said: Abu al-Darda', 'Abd al-'Aziz [ibn Munayb] related to us, who said: Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Kaysan related to us, from his father, from al-Dahhak, Mujahid and Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Five for five." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is five for five?" He said: "No people break a covenant except that their enemy is given power over them; and they do not judge by other than what Allah has revealed except that poverty spreads among them; and indecency does not appear among them except that death spreads among them; and they do not cheat in measure except that they are denied plant growth and are seized by years of drought; and they do not withhold zakat except that rain is withheld from them" [106] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 11/38.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Majah related to us, who said: Ibn Ayyub related to us, who said: al-Qasawani related to us, who said: Sinan ibn Hatim related to us, who said: Hafs related to us, who said: Malik ibn Dinar related to us, who said: I entered upon a neighbour of mine when death had come upon him, and he kept saying: "Two mountains of fire, two mountains of fire." I said: "What are you saying? Are you delirious?"

He said: "O Abu Yahya, I had two measures: I measured with one and took measure with the other." He said: So I got up and began striking one against the other, and he said: "O Abu Yahya, every time you strike one against the other it grows larger," and he died in his pain.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Saqlan related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Naffakh al-Bahili related to us, who said: Barakah ibn Muhammad al-Halabi related to us, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Nadr ibn 'Adi, who said:

I heard 'Ikrima say: "I testify against every measurer or weigher that he is in the Fire." It was said to him: "Your son is a measurer or weigher." He said: "I testify that he is in the Fire."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya al-Qadi related to me, who said: al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us, who said: al-Mubarrad related to us, who said: al-Riyashi related to us, from al-Asma'i, who said: A Bedouin said to me: "Do not seek needs from one whose manliness is at the top of the measures and the teeth of the scales." And 'Abd Khayr related that 'Ali passed by a man who was weighing saffron and had over-weighed it. He tilted the scale and said: "Establish the weighing with justice, then over-weigh afterwards as much as you wish." Nafi' said: Ibn 'Umar used to pass by a seller and say: "Fear Allah and give full measure and weight, for the defrauders will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection until sweat will bridle them up to the middles of their ears."

﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a great Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾? Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Malik related to us, who said: Ibn Hanbal related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Waki' related to us, from Hisham, the companion of [al-Dastawani], from al-Qamar ibn Abi [Abzi], who said: someone who heard Ibn 'Umar recite "Woe to those who give less," when he reached "the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds," wept until they fell down, and he refrained from reciting what followed.

﴿Nay﴾. Al-Hasan said: truly. ﴿Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾: the register in which their deeds are written. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, Mughith ibn Sumayy, Qatada, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: it is the lowest seventh earth, in which are the spirits of the disbelievers and their deeds. What indicates this is what

al-Husayn informed us, who said: Musa related to us, who said: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, who said: Isma'il related to us, who said: al-Musayyib related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sijjin is beneath the seven earths."

[107] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/292; similar in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

And Abu 'Abd Allah al-Fanjawi informed me, who said: Abu 'Ali al-Muqri' related to us, who said: Abu [al-Qasim ibn] al-Fadl related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari related to us, who said: Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Sam'ar ibn 'Atiyya, who said: Ibn 'Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said: "Inform me about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted: 'Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin'." He said: The spirit of the wicked is raised up to the heaven, but the heaven refuses to accept it. Then it is brought down to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it. So it descends beneath the seven earths until it reaches Sijjin, which is the boundary of Iblis. From Sijjin, beneath the boundary of Iblis, there comes out a scroll, which is inscribed and sealed and placed beneath the boundary of Iblis, bearing the knowledge of their ruin until the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also held this view, saying: Sijjin is beneath the boundary of Iblis. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: It is the lowest earth, in which are Iblis and his offspring.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related to us, who said: I read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: 'Imara ibn 'Isa related to me from Yunus ibn Yazid, from one who related to him from Ibn 'Abbas that he said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Inform me about Sijjin and 'Illiyyun." Ka'b said:

"By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will inform you of it only according to what I find in the revealed Book of Allah. As for Sijjin, it is a black tree beneath the seven earths, in which is written every name of a devil. When the soul of the disbeliever is taken, it is raised to the heaven, but the gates of the heaven are shut before it, and then it is thrown down to Sijjin; that is Sijjin. As for 'Illiyyun, when the soul of the Muslim is taken, it is raised to the heaven and the gates of the heaven are opened for it until it reaches the Throne." He said: "Then a palm comes out from the Throne and writes for him his lodging and his honour; that is 'Illiyyun."

Al-Kalbi said: It is a rock beneath the lowest seventh earth, green with the greenness of the heavens, and the book of the wicked is placed beneath it. Wahb said: It is the last domain of Iblis.

'Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa told them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti related to me, who said: Mas'ud ibn Musa ibn Mishkan related to us, who said: Nasr ibn Khuzayma related to us, from Shu'ayb ibn Safwan, from al-Qurti, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Al-Falaq is a well in Hell that is covered, and as for Sijjin, it is a well in Hell that is open." [108] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/120; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/325.]]

Abu al-Qamar al-Saffar informed us, who said: Hajib ibn Ahmad informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us, who said:

Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin." Al-Akhfash said: It is in a narrow, severe prison, and it is of the pattern fa''il from "prison," as one says "fasiq" and "shariyb." Ibn Muqbil said:

"And their companions strike the swords in the bright hour, a striking that the heroes have enjoined upon one another, imprisoning." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ — that is, O Muhammad, what is Sijjin? That is the book that is in Sijjin. Then He explained: ﴿It is a book inscribed﴾: that is, it is a written, recorded book set against them like a mark in a garment, not forgotten and not erased until they are recompensed by it. Qatada said: "marked against them with evil." It was also said: "sealed in the language of Himyar."

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers, who deny the Day of Judgment. None deny it except every transgressor, sinful, who, when Our verses are recited to him, says: "Tales of the ancients."﴾ The common reading is "tutla" (recited); Abu Hayyan read it with the ya', because the verb is placed first.

﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.﴾

We were informed by al-Husayn, who said:

Al-Fadl related to us, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Mukarram al-Tarbi related to us in Baghdad, who said: 'Ali al-Mukarrami related to us, who said: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan say: al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim related to me that Abu Salih al-Sammān said that Abu Hurayra related to him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, when the servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he repents, his heart is polished; if he returns (to sin), it increases until his heart is blackened."

[109] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/297; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 1/25; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/123, with variation.]] He said:

That is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts." And so the exegetes said: it is sin upon sin until the heart is blackened. Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman said: The heart is like the palm; when the servant sins, it contracts and closes one finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes another finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes all its fingers, and then it is sealed. They used to regard that as the "rayn," and then he recited this verse.

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: When the servant commits a sin, it becomes in his heart like the prick of a needle; then when he sins a second time, it becomes like that; when sins multiply, the heart becomes like a sieve or a strainer. al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin, until perhaps it rusts the heart. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He sealed them." 'Ata' said: "They were overcome over their hearts, and so they fell upon them, and so they do not feel alarm or shame." It was also said: "He turned it over, so that its lower part became its upper part," like His saying: "And We turn their hearts about" [[Surat al-An'am: 110.]]. The root of "rayn" is domination; one says: "The wine rayn over his mind" when it overcomes him so that he becomes drunk. Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:

"Then when he sees him, wine has overcome him, and he does not get rid of it by guarding against it."

And the rajiz said:

"We did not drink until I was exiled, and the wine overcame me, and it overcame the cupbearer who was with me."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/122.]]

The meaning of the verse: their hearts were overcome, and it encompassed them until it covered and overwhelmed them.

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 83, verses 1–14:

Makkiyya? No: it is Madaniyya (Medinan), and it has thirty-six verses, one hundred and sixty-nine words, and seven hundred and thirty letters.

We were informed by Kamil ibn Ahmad al-Mufid, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Mutar al-'Adl, who said: Ibn Ibrahim ibn Shurayk al-Asadi related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Yarbu'i related to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, who said: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mutaffifin, Allah, glorified is He, will give him to drink from the sealed wine (al-Raheeq al-Makhtum) on the Day of Resurrection" [105] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/289.]].

[107] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/292; similar in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

Abu Muhammad al-Makhlidi related to us, who said: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr related to us, who said:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Yazid al-Nahwi related to me that 'Ikrima related to him from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, they were among the most dishonest people in measuring. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed "Woe to those who give less," and they improved their measuring.

Al-Qurtubi said: In Medina there were merchants who cheated in measure, and their trade was like gambling, the "munabadha" and "mulamasa" and "mukhatara" (types of forbidden sale). So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the market and recited it to them.

Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, and there was a man there called Abu Juhayna, who had two sa's: he measured with one and took measure with the other. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Yusuf related to us, who said: Ibn 'Imran related to us, who said: Abu al-Darda', 'Abd al-'Aziz [ibn Munayb] related to us, who said: Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Kaysan related to us, from his father, from al-Dahhak, Mujahid and Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Five for five." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is five for five?" He said: "No people break a covenant except that their enemy is given power over them; and they do not judge by other than what Allah has revealed except that poverty spreads among them; and indecency does not appear among them except that death spreads among them; and they do not cheat in measure except that they are denied plant growth and are seized by years of drought; and they do not withhold zakat except that rain is withheld from them" [106] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 11/38.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Majah related to us, who said: Ibn Ayyub related to us, who said: al-Qasawani related to us, who said: Sinan ibn Hatim related to us, who said: Hafs related to us, who said: Malik ibn Dinar related to us, who said: I entered upon a neighbour of mine when death had come upon him, and he kept saying: "Two mountains of fire, two mountains of fire." I said: "What are you saying? Are you delirious?"

He said: "O Abu Yahya, I had two measures: I measured with one and took measure with the other." He said: So I got up and began striking one against the other, and he said: "O Abu Yahya, every time you strike one against the other it grows larger," and he died in his pain.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Saqlan related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Naffakh al-Bahili related to us, who said: Barakah ibn Muhammad al-Halabi related to us, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Nadr ibn 'Adi, who said:

I heard 'Ikrima say: "I testify against every measurer or weigher that he is in the Fire." It was said to him: "Your son is a measurer or weigher." He said: "I testify that he is in the Fire."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya al-Qadi related to me, who said: al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us, who said: al-Mubarrad related to us, who said: al-Riyashi related to us, from al-Asma'i, who said: A Bedouin said to me: "Do not seek needs from one whose manliness is at the top of the measures and the teeth of the scales." And 'Abd Khayr related that 'Ali passed by a man who was weighing saffron and had over-weighed it. He tilted the scale and said: "Establish the weighing with justice, then over-weigh afterwards as much as you wish." Nafi' said: Ibn 'Umar used to pass by a seller and say: "Fear Allah and give full measure and weight, for the defrauders will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection until sweat will bridle them up to the middles of their ears."

﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected for a great Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾? Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Malik related to us, who said: Ibn Hanbal related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Waki' related to us, from Hisham, the companion of [al-Dastawani], from al-Qamar ibn Abi [Abzi], who said: someone who heard Ibn 'Umar recite "Woe to those who give less," when he reached "the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds," wept until they fell down, and he refrained from reciting what followed.

﴿Nay﴾. Al-Hasan said: truly. ﴿Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾: the register in which their deeds are written. 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, Mughith ibn Sumayy, Qatada, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: it is the lowest seventh earth, in which are the spirits of the disbelievers and their deeds. What indicates this is what

al-Husayn informed us, who said: Musa related to us, who said: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, who said: Isma'il related to us, who said: al-Musayyib related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sijjin is beneath the seven earths."

[107] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/292; similar in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

And Abu 'Abd Allah al-Fanjawi informed me, who said: Abu 'Ali al-Muqri' related to us, who said: Abu [al-Qasim ibn] al-Fadl related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari related to us, who said: Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Sam'ar ibn 'Atiyya, who said: Ibn 'Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said: "Inform me about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted: 'Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin'." He said: The spirit of the wicked is raised up to the heaven, but the heaven refuses to accept it. Then it is brought down to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it. So it descends beneath the seven earths until it reaches Sijjin, which is the boundary of Iblis. From Sijjin, beneath the boundary of Iblis, there comes out a scroll, which is inscribed and sealed and placed beneath the boundary of Iblis, bearing the knowledge of their ruin until the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also held this view, saying: Sijjin is beneath the boundary of Iblis. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: It is the lowest earth, in which are Iblis and his offspring.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related to us, who said: I read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: 'Imara ibn 'Isa related to me from Yunus ibn Yazid, from one who related to him from Ibn 'Abbas that he said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Inform me about Sijjin and 'Illiyyun." Ka'b said:

"By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will inform you of it only according to what I find in the revealed Book of Allah. When the soul of the disbeliever is taken, it is raised to the heaven, but the gates of the heaven are shut before it, and then it is thrown down to Sijjin; that is Sijjin. As for 'Illiyyun, when the soul of the Muslim is taken, it is raised to the heaven and the gates of the heaven are opened for it until it reaches the Throne." He said: "Then a palm comes out from the Throne and writes for him his lodging and his honour; that is 'Illiyyun."

Al-Kalbi said: It is a rock beneath the lowest seventh earth, green with the greenness of the heavens, and the book of the wicked is placed beneath it. Wahb said: It is the last domain of Iblis.

'Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa told them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti related to me, who said: Mas'ud ibn Musa ibn Mishkan related to us, who said: Nasr ibn Khuzayma related to us, from Shu'ayb ibn Safwan, from al-Qurti, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Al-Falaq is a well in Hell that is covered, and as for Sijjin, it is a well in Hell that is open." ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.﴾

We were informed by al-Husayn, who said:

Al-Fadl related to us, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Mukarram al-Tarbi related to us in Baghdad, who said: 'Ali al-Mukarrami related to us, who said: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan say: al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim related to me that Abu Salih al-Sammān said that Abu Hurayra related to him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, when the servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he repents, his heart is polished; if he returns (to sin), it increases until his heart is blackened."

[109] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/297; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 1/25; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/123, with variation.]] He said:

That is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts." And so the exegetes said: it is sin upon sin until the heart is blackened. Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman said: The heart is like the palm; when the servant sins, it contracts and closes one finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes another finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes all its fingers, and then it is sealed. They used to regard that as the "rayn," and then he recited this verse.

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: When the servant commits a sin, it becomes in his heart like the prick of a needle; then when he sins a second time, it becomes like that; when sins multiply, the heart becomes like a sieve or a strainer. al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin, until perhaps it rusts the heart. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He sealed them." 'Ata' said: "They were overcome over their hearts, and so they fell upon them, and so they do not feel alarm or shame." It was also said: "He turned it over, so that its lower part became its upper part," like His saying: "And We turn their hearts about" [[Surat al-An'am: 110.]]. The root of "rayn" is domination; one says: "The wine rayn over his mind" when it overcomes him so that he becomes drunk. Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:

"Then when he sees him, wine has overcome him, and he does not get rid of it by guarding against it."

And the rajiz said:

"We did not drink until I was exiled, and the wine overcame me, and it overcame the cupbearer who was with me."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/122.]]

The meaning of the verse: their hearts were overcome, and it encompassed them until it covered and overwhelmed them.

Makkiyya? No: it is Madaniyya (Medinan), and it has thirty-six verses, one hundred and sixty-nine words, and seven hundred and thirty letters.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

If he repents, his heart is polished; if he returns (to sin), it increases until his heart is blackened."

[109] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/297; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 1/25; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/123, with variation.]] He said:

That is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts." And so the exegetes said: it is sin upon sin until the heart is blackened. Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman said: The heart is like the palm; when the servant sins, it contracts and closes one finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes another finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes all its fingers, and then it is sealed. They used to regard that as the "rayn," and then he recited this verse.

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: When the servant commits a sin, it becomes in his heart like the prick of a needle; then when he sins a second time, it becomes like that; when sins multiply, the heart becomes like a sieve or a strainer. al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin, until perhaps it rusts the heart. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He sealed them." 'Ata' said: "They were overcome over their hearts, and so they fell upon them, and so they do not feel alarm or shame." It was also said: "He turned it over, so that its lower part became its upper part," like His saying: "And We turn their hearts about" [[Surat al-An'am: 110.]]. The root of "rayn" is domination; one says: "The wine rayn over his mind" when it overcomes him so that he becomes drunk. Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:

"Then when he sees him, wine has overcome him, and he does not get rid of it by guarding against it."

And the rajiz said:

"We did not drink until I was exiled, and the wine overcame me, and it overcame the cupbearer who was with me."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/122.]]

The meaning of the verse: their hearts were overcome, and it encompassed them until it covered and overwhelmed them.

Commentary of al-Tha'labi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 83, verses 1–14:

Makkiyya? No: it is Madaniyya (Medinan), and it has thirty-six verses, one hundred and sixty-nine words, and seven hundred and thirty letters.

We were informed by Kamil ibn Ahmad al-Mufid, who said: we were informed by Muhammad ibn Mutar al-'Adl, who said: Ibn Ibrahim ibn Shurayk al-Asadi related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Yunus al-Yarbu'i related to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym related to us, who said: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umama, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mutaffifin, Allah, glorified is He, will give him to drink from the sealed wine (al-Raheeq al-Makhtum) on the Day of Resurrection" [105] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/289.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

in the copies of the Qur'an, except for dropping it.

﴿Yukhsirun﴾: they diminish.

Abu Muhammad al-Makhlidi related to us, who said: Ibn al-Sharqi informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr related to us, who said:

'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Yazid al-Nahwi related to me that 'Ikrima related to him from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, they were among the most dishonest people in measuring. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed "Woe to those who give less," and they improved their measuring.

Al-Qurtubi said: In Medina there were merchants who cheated in measure, and their trade was like gambling, the "munabadha" and "mulamasa" and "mukhatara" (types of forbidden sale). So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to the market and recited it to them.

Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Medina, and there was a man there called Abu Juhayna, who had two sa's: he measured with one and took measure with the other. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Yusuf related to us, who said: Ibn 'Imran related to us, who said: Abu al-Darda', 'Abd al-'Aziz [ibn Munayb] related to us, who said: Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Kaysan related to us, from his father, from al-Dahhak, Mujahid and Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Five for five." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is five for five?" He said: "No people break a covenant except that their enemy is given power over them; and they do not judge by other than what Allah has revealed except that poverty spreads among them; and indecency does not appear among them except that death spreads among them; and they do not cheat in measure except that they are denied plant growth and are seized by years of drought; and they do not withhold zakat except that rain is withheld from them" [106] [[al-Mu'jam al-Kabir: 11/38.]].

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Majah related to us, who said: Ibn Ayyub related to us, who said: al-Qasawani related to us, who said: Sinan ibn Hatim related to us, who said: Hafs related to us, who said: Malik ibn Dinar related to us, who said: I entered upon a neighbour of mine when death had come upon him, and he kept saying: "Two mountains of fire, two mountains of fire." I said: "What are you saying? Are you delirious?"

He said: "O Abu Yahya, I had two measures: I measured with one and took measure with the other." He said: So I got up and began striking one against the other, and he said: "O Abu Yahya, every time you strike one against the other it grows larger," and he died in his pain.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Saqlan related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Naffakh al-Bahili related to us, who said: Barakah ibn Muhammad al-Halabi related to us, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Nadr ibn 'Adi, who said:

I heard 'Ikrima say: "I testify against every measurer or weigher that he is in the Fire." It was said to him: "Your son is a measurer or weigher." He said: "I testify that he is in the Fire."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Zakariyya al-Qadi related to me, who said: al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad related to us, who said: al-Mubarrad related to us, who said: al-Riyashi related to us, from al-Asma'i, who said: A Bedouin said to me: "Do not seek needs from one whose manliness is at the top of the measures and the teeth of the scales." And 'Abd Khayr related that 'Ali passed by a man who was weighing saffron and had over-weighed it. He tilted the scale and said: "Establish the weighing with justice, then over-weigh afterwards as much as you wish." Nafi' said: Ibn 'Umar used to pass by a seller and say: "Fear Allah and give full measure and weight, for the defrauders will be made to stand on the Day of Resurrection until sweat will bridle them up to the middles of their ears."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: Ibn Malik related to us, who said: Ibn Hanbal related to us, who said: my father related to me, who said: Waki' related to us, from Hisham, the companion of [al-Dastawani], from al-Qamar ibn Abi [Abzi], who said: someone who heard Ibn 'Umar recite "Woe to those who give less," when he reached "the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds," wept until they fell down, and he refrained from reciting what followed.

al-Husayn informed us, who said: Musa related to us, who said: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us, who said: Isma'il related to us, who said: al-Musayyib related to us, who said: al-A'mash related to us, from al-Minhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Sijjin is beneath the seven earths."

[107] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/292; similar in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

And Abu 'Abd Allah al-Fanjawi informed me, who said: Abu 'Ali al-Muqri' related to us, who said: Abu [al-Qasim ibn] al-Fadl related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari related to us, who said: Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Sam'ar ibn 'Atiyya, who said: Ibn 'Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said: "Inform me about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted: 'Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin'." He said: The spirit of the wicked is raised up to the heaven, but the heaven refuses to accept it. Then it is brought down to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it. So it descends beneath the seven earths until it reaches Sijjin, which is the boundary of Iblis. From Sijjin, beneath the boundary of Iblis, there comes out a scroll, which is inscribed and sealed and placed beneath the boundary of Iblis, bearing the knowledge of their ruin until the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also held this view, saying: Sijjin is beneath the boundary of Iblis. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: It is the lowest earth, in which are Iblis and his offspring.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related to us, who said: I read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: 'Imara ibn 'Isa related to me from Yunus ibn Yazid, from one who related to him from Ibn 'Abbas that he said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Inform me about Sijjin and 'Illiyyun." Ka'b said:

"By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will inform you of it only according to what I find in the revealed Book of Allah. As for Sijjin, it is a black tree beneath the seven earths, in which is written every name of a devil. When the soul of the disbeliever is taken, it is raised to the heaven, but the gates of the heaven are shut before it, and then it is thrown down to Sijjin; that is Sijjin. As for 'Illiyyun, when the soul of the Muslim is taken, it is raised to the heaven and the gates of the heaven are opened for it until it reaches the Throne." He said: "Then a palm comes out from the Throne and writes for him his lodging and his honour; that is 'Illiyyun."

Al-Kalbi said: It is a rock beneath the lowest seventh earth, green with the greenness of the heavens, and the book of the wicked is placed beneath it. Wahb said: It is the last domain of Iblis.

Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin." He said: Sijjin is a rock beneath the seventh earth, turned over, and the record of the wicked is placed beneath it. Ikrima said: That is, they are in loss and error. The meaning is that he intended the nullification of their deeds and their passing away without praise or reward, and this is a common and widespread usage among people: they say of one whose mention has faded and whose standing has fallen: "he has clung to the dust." Al-Akhfash said: It is in a narrow, severe prison, and it is of the pattern fa''il from "prison," as one says "fasiq" and "shariyb." Ibn Muqbil said:

"And their companions strike the swords in the bright hour, a striking that the heroes have enjoined upon one another, imprisoning." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ — that is, O Muhammad, what is Sijjin? That is the book that is in Sijjin. Then He explained: ﴿It is a book inscribed﴾: that is, it is a written, recorded book set against them like a mark in a garment, not forgotten and not erased until they are recompensed by it. Qatada said: "marked against them with evil." It was also said: "sealed in the language of Himyar."

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers, who deny the Day of Judgment. None deny it except every transgressor, sinful, who, when Our verses are recited to him, says: "Tales of the ancients."﴾ The common reading is "tutla" (recited); Abu Hayyan read it with the ya', because the verb is placed first.

﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.﴾

[107] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/292; similar in Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

And Abu 'Abd Allah al-Fanjawi informed me, who said: Abu 'Ali al-Muqri' related to us, who said: Abu [al-Qasim ibn] al-Fadl related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah al-Ash'ari related to us, who said: Hafs ibn Humayd related to us, from Sam'ar ibn 'Atiyya, who said: Ibn 'Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said: "Inform me about the saying of Allah, glorified and exalted: 'Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin'." He said: The spirit of the wicked is raised up to the heaven, but the heaven refuses to accept it. Then it is brought down to the earth, but the earth refuses to accept it. So it descends beneath the seven earths until it reaches Sijjin, which is the boundary of Iblis. From Sijjin, beneath the boundary of Iblis, there comes out a scroll, which is inscribed and sealed and placed beneath the boundary of Iblis, bearing the knowledge of their ruin until the reckoning of the Day of Resurrection. Sa'id ibn Jubayr also held this view, saying: Sijjin is beneath the boundary of Iblis. 'Ata' al-Khurasani said: It is the lowest earth, in which are Iblis and his offspring.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, who said: al-Fadl related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hatim related to us, who said: I read to Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: 'Imara ibn 'Isa related to me from Yunus ibn Yazid, from one who related to him from Ibn 'Abbas that he said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: "Inform me about Sijjin and 'Illiyyun." Ka'b said:

"By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will inform you of it only according to what I find in the revealed Book of Allah. As for Sijjin, it is a black tree beneath the seven earths, in which is written every name of a devil. When the soul of the disbeliever is taken, it is raised to the heaven, but the gates of the heaven are shut before it, and then it is thrown down to Sijjin; that is Sijjin. As for 'Illiyyun, when the soul of the Muslim is taken, it is raised to the heaven and the gates of the heaven are opened for it until it reaches the Throne." He said: "Then a palm comes out from the Throne and writes for him his lodging and his honour; that is 'Illiyyun."

Al-Kalbi said: It is a rock beneath the lowest seventh earth, green with the greenness of the heavens, and the book of the wicked is placed beneath it. Wahb said: It is the last domain of Iblis.

'Aqil informed me that al-Mu'afa told them, from Ibn Jarir, who said: Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti related to me, who said: Mas'ud ibn Musa ibn Mishkan related to us, who said: Nasr ibn Khuzayma related to us, from Shu'ayb ibn Safwan, from al-Qurti, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Al-Falaq is a well in Hell that is covered, and as for Sijjin, it is a well in Hell that is open." [108] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/120; al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/325.]]

Abu al-Qamar al-Saffar informed us, who said: Hajib ibn Ahmad informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us, who said:

Yahya ibn Sulaym al-Ta'ifi related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Indeed the record of the wicked is in Sijjin." He said: Sijjin is a rock beneath the seventh earth, turned over, and the record of the wicked is placed beneath it. Ikrima said: That is, they are in loss and error. The meaning is that he intended the nullification of their deeds and their passing away without praise or reward, and this is a common and widespread usage among people: they say of one whose mention has faded and whose standing has fallen: "he has clung to the dust." Al-Akhfash said: It is in a narrow, severe prison, and it is of the pattern fa''il from "prison," as one says "fasiq" and "shariyb." Ibn Muqbil said:

"And their companions strike the swords in the bright hour, a striking that the heroes have enjoined upon one another, imprisoning." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/258.]]

﴿And what will make you know what Sijjin is?﴾ — that is, O Muhammad, what is Sijjin? That is the book that is in Sijjin. Then He explained: ﴿It is a book inscribed﴾: that is, it is a written, recorded book set against them like a mark in a garment, not forgotten and not erased until they are recompensed by it. Qatada said: "marked against them with evil." It was also said: "sealed in the language of Himyar."

﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers, who deny the Day of Judgment. None deny it except every transgressor, sinful, who, when Our verses are recited to him, says: "Tales of the ancients."﴾ The common reading is "tutla" (recited); Abu Hayyan read it with the ya', because the verb is placed first.

﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts.﴾

We were informed by al-Husayn, who said:

Al-Fadl related to us, who said: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Mukarram al-Tarbi related to us in Baghdad, who said: 'Ali al-Mukarrami related to us, who said: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan say: al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim related to me that Abu Salih al-Sammān said that Abu Hurayra related to him that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Indeed, when the servant commits a sin, a black spot is placed on his heart. If he repents, his heart is polished; if he returns (to sin), it increases until his heart is blackened."

[109] [[Musnad Ahmad: 2/297; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 1/25; Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/123, with variation.]] He said:

That is the saying of Allah, glorified is He: "Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has rusted over their hearts." And so the exegetes said: it is sin upon sin until the heart is blackened. Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman said: The heart is like the palm; when the servant sins, it contracts and closes one finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes another finger, then when he sins again, it contracts and closes all its fingers, and then it is sealed. They used to regard that as the "rayn," and then he recited this verse.

Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: When the servant commits a sin, it becomes in his heart like the prick of a needle; then when he sins a second time, it becomes like that; when sins multiply, the heart becomes like a sieve or a strainer. al-Hasan said: It is sin upon sin, until perhaps it rusts the heart. Ibn 'Abbas said: "He sealed them." 'Ata' said: "They were overcome over their hearts, and so they fell upon them, and so they do not feel alarm or shame." It was also said: "He turned it over, so that its lower part became its upper part," like His saying: "And We turn their hearts about" [[Surat al-An'am: 110.]]. The root of "rayn" is domination; one says: "The wine rayn over his mind" when it overcomes him so that he becomes drunk. Abu Zubayd al-Ta'i said:

"Then when he sees him, wine has overcome him, and he does not get rid of it by guarding against it."

And the rajiz said:

"We did not drink until I was exiled, and the wine overcame me, and it overcame the cupbearer who was with me."

[[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 30/122.]]

The meaning of the verse: their hearts were overcome, and it encompassed them until it covered and overwhelmed them.

﴿Nay, indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾ Some of them said: they will be barred from His generosity and mercy. Qatadah said: it means that He will not look at them... ﴿nor purify them﴾. Most exegetes said: they will be barred from seeing Him. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Just as He veiled them in this world from knowing His oneness, He veils them in the Hereafter from seeing Him.

We were told by al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Hani told us, who said:

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl told us, who said: Affan ibn Muslim al-Saffar told us, from al-Rabi' ibn Subayh and Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd, who both said: al-Hasan said: If the ascetics and the worshippers knew that they would not see their Lord in the Return, their souls would depart in this world.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad say: I heard Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Ahmad [al-Shabuwi] [[So in the manuscript.]] say: I heard Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi say: I heard al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman say: One day I was with al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, and a letter came to him from Upper Egypt asking him about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾ He wrote in reply: "That He veiled a people in wrath indicates that a people will see Him in pleasure." I said to him: "Do you hold this opinion, my master?"

He said: "By Allah, if Muhammad ibn Idris did not believe with certainty that he would see his Lord in the Return, he would not have worshipped Him in this world."

﴿Then indeed they will surely burn in Hellfire.﴾ Surely they will enter the Fire. ﴿Then it will be said: This is what you used to deny.﴾ ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn.﴾

Al-Husayn told me, who said: Musa told us, who said: Ibn Alawiyyah told us, who said: Isma'il told us, who said: al-Musayyib told us, from al-A'mash, from al-Nahhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "ʿIlliyyūn is in the seventh heaven, beneath the Throne." [110] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/262.]]

Ibn Abbas said: It is a tablet of green emerald suspended beneath the Throne, in which their deeds are written. Ka'b and Qatadah said: It is the right pillar of the Throne. Muqatil said: It is the leg of the Throne. Ali ibn Abi Talhah and Ata, from Ibn Abbas, said: It is Paradise. Atiyyah, from him, said: Their deeds are in the Book of Allah in the heaven. al-Dahhak said: It is the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha). The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: It is height upon height and honour upon honour. For this reason it was formed with the plural suffix -ūn and -īn, as with masculine plurals when the word has no singular from its own root or no dual form. Al-Farra' said: It is a noun formed in the pattern of a plural, having no singular from its own form, like saying ʿishrīn and thalathīn. Yunus al-Nahwi said: Its singular is ʿallī and ʿalliyyah.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me, who said: Ibn Hamdan told us, who said: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Malhami told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yunus told us, who said: Affan told us, who said: Affan told us, who said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Khaythamah, from Abdullah ibn Amr, regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn.﴾ He said: The people of ʿIlliyyūn look down upon the people of Paradise from such-and-such a place. When a man appears above them, Paradise lights up, and they say: "A man from the people of ʿIlliyyūn has risen above us."

﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is? It is a written record, witnessed by those brought near.﴾ It was written for him with good. In the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir); its meaning is:

"Indeed the record of the righteous is written in ʿIlliyyūn, which is the place of the angels. Similarly, indeed the record of the wicked is a written record, and it is Sijjīn, which is the place of Iblis and his armies."

﴿Witnessed by those brought near﴾ — the angels. ﴿Indeed the righteous will be in bliss, upon couches, looking on﴾ — that is, what Allah, the Exalted, has given them of honour and blessing. The arā'ik (couches) are everything one reclines upon. It was said: a bed within a canopy. Muqatil said: they look upon their enemies to see how they are punished. Ibn Ata said: "Upon couches of knowledge they look upon the Known; and upon couches of nearness they look upon the Kind One."

﴿You will recognise in their faces the radiance of bliss.﴾ That is, its essence, its sheen and its light. It is said: anḍara al-nabat when it blossomed and bloomed. The common reading is taʿrifu with a fatha on the ta and a kasra on the ra, and nadrata (the radiance) is in the accusative. Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ta and a fatha on the ra, in the passive voice (ghayr tasmiyat al-fa'il).

﴿They will be given to drink of sealed wine (raḥīq)﴾ — pure, good wine. It was said: it is aged wine. Muqatil said: white wine.

Hassan said:
"They are given to drink from the water of al-Barisad upon them,
a cool drink mixed with the flowing raḥīq."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

Another said:
"Or is there no path to youth and its remembrance,
more delightful to me than the flowing raḥīq?"
[[Lisan al-Arab: 11/343.]]

﴿Sealed﴾ — it has been sealed and kept from being touched by anyone or reached by any hand until its seal is broken by the righteous on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: "sealed with clay" (mutayyan).

﴿Its seal is musk﴾ — Ibn Zayd said: its seal with Allah, the Exalted, is musk, and its seal in this world is clay. Ibn Mas'ud said: "sealed, mixed": its seal is a blend and musk. Alqamah said: its taste and its scent are musk. Others said: its final outcome and its last taste is musk. Qatadah said: it is mixed for them with camphor and sealed with musk. Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit related from Abu al-Darda', regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Its seal is musk﴾, that he said: "It is a white drink like silver, with which they seal their drinking. Were a man of this world to put his finger into it and then withdraw it, no living soul would remain without smelling its fragrance."

The sealing (khatm) of everything is its completion; from it comes the expression "the completion of the Qur'an" and "deeds are judged by their endings" (al-a'mal bi-khawatimiha). The common reading is khitāmuhu with the ta' placed first.

Al-Kisa'i read khātimuhu, which is the reading of Ali and Alqamah.

Muhammad ibn Abdus told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm told us, who said: Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra' told us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl told me, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, that he read khātimuhu misk.

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its parallel is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For the like of this let the workers work.﴾ [[Surat al-Sajdah: 17.]] Muqatil ibn Sulayman: let those who compete, compete. Ibn Hayyan: let those who hasten, hasten. Ata: let those who race, race. Zayd ibn Aslam: let those who are eager, be eager. Ibn Jarir: let them strive for it and be keen upon it. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. Muqatil: it is called Tasnim because it is raised (yatasannam) and poured down upon them from above, in their chambers and dwellings, flowing from the Garden of Eden to the people of the Gardens. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas said: it is pure for the nearest ones (muqarrabun), who drink it unmixed, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise.

Abdullah ibn Hamid, with others, told us, who said: Makki told us, who said: Ammar ibn Raja' told us, who said: Suwayd ibn Amr al-Kalbi told us, who said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yunus ibn Maysarah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾, that he said: "This is of what Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾" [[Surat al-Saffat: 61.]] And from some of them: it is a spring flowing in the air, raised high, poured into the vessels of the people of Paradise according to the measure of their filling. When they are full, the water is held back so that not a drop falls to the ground, and they have no need to draw water. This is the meaning of Qatadah's words. The root of the word is from the height of a place and its standing, so a raised thing is called sanam, and a noble man is called sanam. It is a proper noun, like al-Tan'im, which is the name of a mountain.

﴿A spring from which the nearest ones drink﴾ — that is, from it. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

﴿Indeed those who committed crimes﴾ — they associated partners with Allah: Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-As ibn Wa'il and their companions, from the affluent of Mecca. ﴿Used to laugh at those who believed﴾ — Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal and their companions, from the poor believers.

﴿Laughing﴾ — mocking them and wondering at their Islam.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. He came with a group of Muslims to the Prophet ﷺ, and the hypocrites mocked them, laughed and winked at one another. Then they returned to their companions and said: "Today we saw the bald one (al-asla'), and we laughed at him." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed these verses before Ali and his companions reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [111] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/298, and similar in Shawahid al-Tanzil 2: 428.]]

﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

﴿So today﴾ — that is, the Day of Resurrection — ﴿those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾, just as the disbelievers laughed at them in the world. That is because a door to Paradise will be opened for the disbelievers, and it will be said to them: "Come out to it." When they reach it, it will be shut in their faces. This will be done to them repeatedly, and the believers will laugh at them, while they are ﴿upon couches﴾ of pearl and ruby, ﴿looking on﴾ at them, watching how they are punished. Ka'b said: between Paradise and the Fire there are openings; when a believer wishes to look upon an enemy he had in the world, he looks out through one of those openings. Its evidence is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 55.]]

﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid (hal thuwwiba) for what they used to do?﴾ — thuwwiba means "was recompensed" (jutiziya), and thawwaba and athaba have the same meaning.

﴿Nay, indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾ Some of them said: they will be barred from His generosity and mercy. Qatadah said: it means that He will not look at them... ﴿nor purify them﴾. Most exegetes said: they will be barred from seeing Him. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: Just as He veiled them in this world from knowing His oneness, He veils them in the Hereafter from seeing Him.

We were told by al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far, who said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Hani told us, who said:

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl told us, who said: Affan ibn Muslim al-Saffar told us, from al-Rabi' ibn Subayh and Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd, who both said: al-Hasan said: If the ascetics and the worshippers knew that they would not see their Lord in the Return, their souls would depart in this world.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad say: I heard Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Ahmad [al-Shabuwi] [[So in the manuscript.]] say: I heard Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi say: I heard al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman say: One day I was with al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, and a letter came to him from Upper Egypt asking him about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾ He wrote in reply: "That He veiled a people in wrath indicates that a people will see Him in pleasure." I said to him: "Do you hold this opinion, my master?"

He said: "By Allah, if Muhammad ibn Idris did not believe with certainty that he would see his Lord in the Return, he would not have worshipped Him in this world."

﴿Then indeed they will surely burn in Hellfire.﴾ Surely they will enter the Fire. ﴿Then it will be said: This is what you used to deny.﴾ ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn.﴾

Al-Husayn told me, who said: Musa told us, who said: Ibn Alawiyyah told us, who said: Isma'il told us, who said: al-Musayyib told us, from al-A'mash, from al-Nahhal, from Zadhan, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "ʿIlliyyūn is in the seventh heaven, beneath the Throne." [110] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/262.]]

Ibn Abbas said: It is a tablet of green emerald suspended beneath the Throne, in which their deeds are written. Ka'b and Qatadah said: It is the right pillar of the Throne. Muqatil said: It is the leg of the Throne. Ali ibn Abi Talhah and Ata, from Ibn Abbas, said: It is Paradise. Atiyyah, from him, said: Their deeds are in the Book of Allah in the heaven. al-Dahhak said: It is the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha). The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: It is height upon height and honour upon honour. For this reason it was formed with the plural suffix -ūn and -īn, as with masculine plurals when the word has no singular from its own root or no dual form. Al-Farra' said: It is a noun formed in the pattern of a plural, having no singular from its own form, like saying ʿishrīn and thalathīn. Yunus al-Nahwi said: Its singular is ʿallī and ʿalliyyah.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me, who said: Ibn Hamdan told us, who said: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Malhami told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yunus told us, who said: Affan told us, who said: Affan told us, who said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Khaythamah, from Abdullah ibn Amr, regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, indeed the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn.﴾ He said: The people of ʿIlliyyūn look down upon the people of Paradise from such-and-such a place. When a man appears above them, Paradise lights up, and they say: "A man from the people of ʿIlliyyūn has risen above us."

﴿And what will make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is? It is a written record, witnessed by those brought near.﴾ It was written for him with good. In the verse there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir); its meaning is:

"Indeed the record of the righteous is written in ʿIlliyyūn, which is the place of the angels. Similarly, indeed the record of the wicked is a written record, and it is Sijjīn, which is the place of Iblis and his armies."

﴿Witnessed by those brought near﴾ — the angels. ﴿Indeed the righteous will be in bliss, upon couches, looking on﴾ — that is, what Allah, the Exalted, has given them of honour and blessing. The arā'ik (couches) are everything one reclines upon. It was said: a bed within a canopy. Muqatil said: they look upon their enemies to see how they are punished. Ibn Ata said: "Upon couches of knowledge they look upon the Known; and upon couches of nearness they look upon the Kind One."

﴿You will recognise in their faces the radiance of bliss.﴾ That is, its essence, its sheen and its light. It is said: anḍara al-nabat when it blossomed and bloomed. The common reading is taʿrifu with a fatha on the ta and a kasra on the ra, and nadrata (the radiance) is in the accusative. Abu Ja'far and Ya'qub read it with a damma on the ta and a fatha on the ra, in the passive voice (ghayr tasmiyat al-fa'il).

﴿They will be given to drink of sealed wine (raḥīq)﴾ — pure, good wine. It was said: it is aged wine. Muqatil said: white wine.

Hassan said:
"They are given to drink from the water of al-Barisad upon them,
a cool drink mixed with the flowing raḥīq."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

Another said:
"Or is there no path to youth and its remembrance,
more delightful to me than the flowing raḥīq?"
[[Lisan al-Arab: 11/343.]]

﴿Sealed﴾ — it has been sealed and kept from being touched by anyone or reached by any hand until its seal is broken by the righteous on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: "sealed with clay" (mutayyan).

﴿Its seal is musk﴾ — Ibn Zayd said: its seal with Allah, the Exalted, is musk, and its seal in this world is clay. Ibn Mas'ud said: "sealed, mixed": its seal is a blend and musk. And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him.
