﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. ﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

Yahya ibn Sulayman ibn Nadhlah said: Malik ibn Anas was asked about this verse, and he said:

"He veiled His enemies from Him, so they did not see Him; He manifested Himself to His friends until they saw Him."

[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/143. al-Barīṣ: a river in Damascus; Barada: also a river in Damascus. Yusaffaq: mixed. Raḥīq: white wine.]]

﴿Sealed﴾ — it has been sealed and kept from being touched by anyone or reached by any hand until its seal is broken by the righteous on the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: "sealed with clay" (mutayyan).

﴿Its seal is musk﴾ — Ibn Zayd said: its seal with Allah, the Exalted, is musk, and its seal in this world is clay. Ibn Mas'ud said: "sealed, mixed": its seal is a blend and musk. Alqamah said: its taste and its scent are musk. Others said: its final outcome and its last taste is musk. Qatadah said: it is mixed for them with camphor and sealed with musk. Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit related from Abu al-Darda', regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Its seal is musk﴾, that he said: "It is a white drink like silver, with which they seal their drinking. Were a man of this world to put his finger into it and then withdraw it, no living soul would remain without smelling its fragrance."

The sealing (khatm) of everything is its completion; from it comes the expression "the completion of the Qur'an" and "deeds are judged by their endings" (al-a'mal bi-khawatimiha). The common reading is khitāmuhu with the ta' placed first.

Al-Kisa'i read khātimuhu, which is the reading of Ali and Alqamah.

Muhammad ibn Abdus told us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub told us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Jahm told us, who said: Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra' told us, who said: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl told me, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, that he read khātimuhu misk.

And with his chain, from al-Farra', who said: Abu al-Ahwas told me, from Ash'ath ibn Abi al-Sha'tha' al-Muharibi, who said:

Alqamah ibn Qays read "khātimuhu misk" and said: "Have you not seen the woman who says to the perfumer, 'Make for me its khātim musk,' meaning its end?" The khātim and the khitām are one, just as a noble man is called al-ṭābiʿ and al-ṭibāʿ. Al-Farazdaq said:
"So they spent the night beside me, bolted,
and I spent the night loosening the locks of the khitām."
[[Lisan al-Arab: 10/291.]]

﴿And for this let those who strive, strive﴾ — let those who desire, desire, by hastening to obey Allah. Mujahid said: let those who work, work. Its parallel is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿For the like of this let the workers work.﴾ [[Surat al-Sajdah: 17.]] Muqatil ibn Sulayman: let those who compete, compete. Ibn Hayyan: let those who hasten, hasten. Ata: let those who race, race. Zayd ibn Aslam: let those who are eager, be eager. Ibn Jarir: let them strive for it and be keen upon it. Its root is from a precious thing, which people's souls are keen upon, which each of them seeks, desires and wishes for himself, and begrudges to others (yunfisu bihi ʿala ghayrihi), that is, withholds it.

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ — a drink poured from above. From it comes the hump (sanam) of a camel and the raised graves (tasnim al-qubur). al-Dahhak said: it is a drink called Tasnim, and it is the most noble of drinks. Muqatil: it is called Tasnim because it is raised (yatasannam) and poured down upon them from above, in their chambers and dwellings, flowing from the Garden of Eden to the people of the Gardens. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas said: it is pure for the nearest ones (muqarrabun), who drink it unmixed, and it is mixed for the rest of the people of Paradise.

Abdullah ibn Hamid, with others, told us, who said: Makki told us, who said: Ammar ibn Raja' told us, who said: Suwayd ibn Amr al-Kalbi told us, who said: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yunus ibn Maysarah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾, that he said: "This is of what Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for the eyes.﴾" [[Surat al-Saffat: 61.]] And from some of them: it is a spring flowing in the air, raised high, poured into the vessels of the people of Paradise according to the measure of their filling. When they are full, the water is held back so that not a drop falls to the ground, and they have no need to draw water. This is the meaning of Qatadah's words. The root of the word is from the height of a place and its standing, so a raised thing is called sanam, and a noble man is called sanam. It is a proper noun, like al-Tan'im, which is the name of a mountain.

﴿A spring from which the nearest ones drink﴾ — that is, from it. It was said: the muqarrabun drink it. al-Hariri and al-Wasiti said: "from which the nearest ones drink unmixed, upon the carpet of nearness, in the assembly of intimacy, and the gardens of holiness, with the cup of pleasure, in contemplation of the Truth, the Exalted and Majestic."

﴿Indeed those who committed crimes﴾ — they associated partners with Allah: Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-As ibn Wa'il and their companions, from the affluent of Mecca. ﴿Used to laugh at those who believed﴾ — Ammar, Khabbab, Suhayb, Bilal and their companions, from the poor believers.

﴿Laughing﴾ — mocking them and wondering at their Islam.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him. He came with a group of Muslims to the Prophet ﷺ, and the hypocrites mocked them, laughed and winked at one another. Then they returned to their companions and said: "Today we saw the bald one (al-asla'), and we laughed at him." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed these verses before Ali and his companions reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [111] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/298, and similar in Shawahid al-Tanzil 2: 428.]]

﴿And when they passed by them, they winked at one another.﴾

[They] wink at some and gesture with their eyes. ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting.﴾ ﴿And when they saw them, they said: "Indeed these are astray,"﴾ — when they came to Muhammad, they thought they were upon something. ﴿Yet they were not sent as guardians over them﴾ — that is, the polytheists were not sent over the believers as guardians ﴿over them﴾, meaning over the believers, to watch their deeds, appointed over their conditions.

﴿So today﴾ — that is, the Day of Resurrection — ﴿those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾, just as the disbelievers laughed at them in the world. That is because a door to Paradise will be opened for the disbelievers, and it will be said to them: "Come out to it." When they reach it, it will be shut in their faces. This will be done to them repeatedly, and the believers will laugh at them, while they are ﴿upon couches﴾ of pearl and ruby, ﴿looking on﴾ at them, watching how they are punished. Ka'b said: between Paradise and the Fire there are openings; when a believer wishes to look upon an enemy he had in the world, he looks out through one of those openings. Its evidence is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So he looked and saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire.﴾ [[Surat al-Saffat: 55.]]

﴿Have the disbelievers been repaid (hal thuwwiba) for what they used to do?﴾ — thuwwiba means "was recompensed" (jutiziya), and thawwaba and athaba have the same meaning.
